name: Nitrogen Deficiency
symptoms: Pale-green to yellow lower leaves first (oldest leaves)
General stunted growth and small leaves
Premature leaf drop on chronically deficient plants
Yellowing starts at leaf tips and progresses inward
commonCauses: Sandy soils with low organic matter
Heavy rainfall leaching nitrate from root zone
Imbalanced fertilisation (e.g. heavy K with no N)
treatment: Side-dress with urea (46-0-0) or NPK 17-17-17
Foliar urea spray (1-2%) for fast correction
Apply compost or aged manure
Plant a green-manure cover crop in fallow
prevention: Rotate with N-fixing legumes (cowpea, soybean, beans)
Split nitrogen application — never one heavy dose
Avoid bare fallow that loses N to leaching
severityGuidance: Medium when only lowest leaves yellowed; High when whole-plant chlorosis and stunting
farmerFriendlySummary: Plants look pale and small because they need more nitrogen. Add urea or manure now.

name: Phosphorus Deficiency
symptoms: Dark green or purplish-red discoloration on undersides of leaves
Reduced flowering and poor seed/fruit set
commonCauses: Acidic soils (pH below 5.5) — P locked up
Highly weathered tropical soils naturally low in P
Lack of organic matter for P cycling
treatment: Apply single superphosphate (SSP) or DAP at planting
Lime acidic soils to raise pH toward 6.0-6.5
Incorporate compost rich in P
Mycorrhizal inoculants to improve P uptake
prevention: Place P fertiliser in furrow, not broadcast (high fixation soils)
severityGuidance: Medium when purpling only on edges; High when whole leaves purple and plant stunted
farmerFriendlySummary: Leaves are turning purple — the plant cannot get enough phosphorus. Test soil pH and add SSP or DAP.

name: Potassium Deficiency
symptoms: Yellowing then brown scorching on leaf margins of older leaves
Poor fruit quality — small, soft, low sugar
commonCauses: Sandy soils with low cation exchange capacity
Heavy nitrogen fertilisation without K balance
treatment: Side-dress muriate of potash (MOP) or sulphate of potash (SOP)
Foliar K spray (potassium nitrate) for rapid correction
Apply wood ash (1-2 tons/ha) — naturally K-rich
prevention: Annual soil test for K reserves
Retain crop residues — they recycle K
Mulch to reduce drought stress on K uptake
severityGuidance: Medium when only leaf edges scorched; High when whole leaves brown and stems weak
farmerFriendlySummary: Leaf edges are scorching — plant needs more potassium. Apply MOP or wood ash.

name: Calcium Deficiency
symptoms: Blossom-end rot on tomato, pepper, watermelon (dark sunken spot)
Tip burn on lettuce, cabbage, strawberry
Distorted new growth and hooked leaf tips
Internal browning of bulb / heart vegetables
commonCauses: Uneven watering — drought followed by heavy rain
Acidic soils with low Ca reserves
Heavy ammonium-N fertilisation suppressing Ca uptake
treatment: Foliar calcium chloride spray (0.5%) at first symptoms
Apply gypsum to soil (CaSO4) — doesn't shift pH
Drip irrigation to maintain even soil moisture
Mulch to stabilise soil moisture
prevention: Lime acidic soils before planting (raises Ca + pH)
severityGuidance: Medium when only first fruits show blossom-end rot; High when whole-plant tip burn
farmerFriendlySummary: Dark spots on the bottom of tomatoes or burnt leaf tips mean the plant cannot get calcium. Water evenly and add gypsum.

name: Magnesium Deficiency
symptoms: Yellow patches between green leaf veins (interveinal chlorosis)
Leaves may develop red or purple tints in some species
commonCauses: Sandy, acidic soils naturally low in Mg
Heavy K fertilisation antagonising Mg uptake
Continuous use of high-Ca lime without Mg
Leaching from heavy rainfall in tropical soils
treatment: Foliar Epsom salt spray (MgSO4·7H2O) at 1-2% — fast acting
Apply dolomitic lime (raises Mg + pH)
Side-dress magnesium sulphate (Mg-S)
prevention: Use dolomite instead of calcitic lime when raising pH
Maintain organic matter for Mg cycling
severityGuidance: Medium when interveinal chlorosis only on older leaves; High when whole-plant chlorosis
farmerFriendlySummary: Yellow patches between leaf veins mean magnesium is low. Spray Epsom salt solution.

name: Sulfur Deficiency
symptoms: Uniform pale-yellow new leaves (looks like N deficiency)
Reduced protein content in seeds and forage
Older leaves stay green initially — opposite of N
commonCauses: Sandy soils with low organic matter
Reduced atmospheric S deposition due to clean-air laws
treatment: Apply ammonium sulphate (21-0-0+24S)
Side-dress single superphosphate (contains S)
Gypsum if Ca also low
Foliar magnesium sulphate addresses both Mg and S
prevention: Use S-containing fertilisers in S-deficient regions
Avoid sulphur-free fertilisers like urea alone
severityGuidance: Medium when only young leaves pale; High when whole plant chlorotic
farmerFriendlySummary: New leaves look pale and yellow — plant needs sulphur. Apply ammonium sulphate.

name: Iron Deficiency
symptoms: Yellow leaves with sharp green veins (interveinal chlorosis) on YOUNG leaves
Severe cases: whole new leaves white or cream
commonCauses: Alkaline soils (pH above 7.5) — Fe locked in unavailable form
Heavy calcareous soils common across African Sahel and US Southwest
treatment: Foliar iron chelate (Fe-EDDHA on alkaline soils, Fe-EDTA on neutral) — fast acting
Acidify soil with elemental sulphur (slow)
Apply chelated Fe to soil for long-term correction
Improve drainage if waterlogged
prevention: Use Fe-EDDHA on calcareous soils — only chelate stable above pH 7
Maintain organic matter for natural Fe cycling
severityGuidance: Medium when only top leaves yellow with green veins; High when whole new growth white
farmerFriendlySummary: Young leaves are yellow with green veins — the plant cannot get iron. Spray iron chelate.

name: Zinc Deficiency
symptoms: Small narrow leaves clustered at growing tips ('little leaf', 'rosetting')
Yellow streaking between veins on maize and citrus
commonCauses: Alkaline soils (pH above 7) — Zn locked up
Cold wet soils reducing root uptake
Sandy soils naturally low in Zn
treatment: Foliar zinc sulphate spray (0.5%) — most cost-effective
Soil application of zinc sulphate at planting
Seed treatment with Zn for cereal crops
Compost rich in Zn-containing residues
prevention: Crop rotation away from continuous cereals
severityGuidance: Medium when only some leaves small; High when whole plant rosetted
farmerFriendlySummary: Leaves are small and bunched at the tips — plant needs zinc. Spray zinc sulphate.

name: Boron Deficiency
symptoms: Death of growing tips and lateral buds
Heart rot in beets and brassicas
Poor pollen development and fruit set
commonCauses: Sandy soils with low organic matter
treatment: Foliar borax spray (0.1-0.2%) — VERY narrow window between deficiency and toxicity
Side-dress borax at recommended low rate (per crop label)
Application via fertigation for precision
prevention: Soil test B every 3 years — critical given narrow safe-application range
Use B-containing micronutrient blends in B-deficient regions
severityGuidance: Medium when only growing tips affected; High when widespread plant distortion and hollow stems
farmerFriendlySummary: Growing tips are dying and stems are hollow — plant needs boron. Spray borax carefully (low dose).

name: Copper Deficiency
symptoms: Wilting and dieback of young shoots
Pale and wilting leaves on new growth
Poor pollen viability and seed set
commonCauses: Peat or muck soils (organic complexes bind Cu)
Heavy N fertilisation increasing Cu demand
treatment: Foliar copper sulphate spray (0.1-0.2%)
Copper oxychloride application (also fungicidal)
Soil broadcast of copper sulphate at low rate
Avoid over-application (Cu toxicity easy)
prevention: Soil test for micronutrients every 3 years
Avoid excessive N without Cu balance
Use Cu-containing fungicides in deficient regions
severityGuidance: Medium when only tips wilt; High when whole-plant dieback and seed set affected
farmerFriendlySummary: Young shoots are wilting and dying back — plant needs copper. Spray copper sulphate.

name: Manganese Deficiency
symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis (similar to Fe deficiency) on younger leaves
Grey or olive-green spots on cereal leaves
commonCauses: Cold wet conditions reducing root uptake
treatment: Foliar manganese sulphate spray (0.1-0.2%)
Mn-EDTA chelate on alkaline soils
Acidify soil to pH 6.0-6.5
severityGuidance: Medium when only mild interveinal chlorosis; High when whole-plant chlorosis
farmerFriendlySummary: Young leaves are yellow between veins (like iron deficiency) — plant may need manganese. Spray manganese sulphate.

name: Molybdenum Deficiency
symptoms: Whiptail symptom on cauliflower and broccoli (narrow distorted leaves)
commonCauses: Acidic soils (pH below 5.5) — Mo locked up
Sandy soils naturally low in Mo
treatment: Foliar sodium molybdate (0.1%) — very low rate
Lime acidic soils to raise pH toward 6.5
Seed treatment with Mo for legumes
prevention: Use Mo-containing micronutrient blends in deficient regions
severityGuidance: Medium when only legume nodulation reduced; High when whiptail or whole-plant chlorosis
farmerFriendlySummary: Plant looks like it needs nitrogen but adding nitrogen isn't helping — likely molybdenum deficiency. Lime the soil and spray sodium molybdate.

name: Chloride Deficiency
symptoms: Wilting of leaves even when soil is moist
Chlorosis and bronzing on younger leaves
Rare in field crops; more common in palms and coconut
commonCauses: Sandy inland soils far from sea (atmospheric Cl deposition low)
Use of Cl-free fertilisers (sulphate of potash, ammonium nitrate)
treatment: Side-dress potassium chloride (KCl/MOP)
Apply ammonium chloride if Cl-only needed
Foliar KCl spray for fast correction
prevention: Use Cl-containing K fertiliser (MOP) where Cl-deficient
severityGuidance: Low to Medium — rare in most field crops
farmerFriendlySummary: Plants are wilting even with enough water — sometimes a chloride issue. Use MOP fertiliser.

name: Nickel Deficiency
symptoms: Leaf tip burn on cereals and pecan
treatment: Foliar nickel sulphate spray (very low rate)
Soil amendment with composted residues
Adjust soil pH toward 6.0
prevention: Soil test for Ni in suspected deficient zones
severityGuidance: Low — rarely seen except in pecan and intensive cereal systems
farmerFriendlySummary: Leaf tips are burning on cereals or nuts — could be nickel deficiency. Confirm with soil test.

name: Silicon Deficiency
symptoms: Increased susceptibility to fungal diseases (rice blast, powdery mildew)
Weak stems prone to lodging in rice and cereals
commonCauses: Continuous rice cropping without Si return
Removal of crop residues which would otherwise recycle Si
treatment: Apply calcium silicate slag (steel-mill byproduct) where available
Diatomaceous earth as soil amendment
Retain rice straw to recycle Si
Potassium silicate foliar spray for quick fixes
prevention: Return crop residues to the field
Periodic Si amendment in continuous rice systems
severityGuidance: Medium for rice and cereals — disease pressure increases with deficiency
farmerFriendlySummary: Crops weak-stemmed and disease-prone — silicon helps strengthen plants. Return straw to the field.

name: Iron Toxicity (rice)
symptoms: Bronze spots on rice leaves spreading to whole leaf
Brown root rot and limp roots
Severe yield loss in flooded rice (10-100%)
commonCauses: Flooded acidic soils releasing reduced Fe2+
Inland valley swamps and acid sulphate soils
Continuous lowland rice on poorly-drained sites
treatment: Drain field briefly to oxidise Fe (cautious — affects yield)
Apply lime to raise soil pH
Use Fe-tolerant rice varieties (Suakoko 8, WITA 1)
Phosphate application to compete with Fe in roots
prevention: Plant Fe-tolerant rice varieties on suspect sites
Maintain pH near neutral with lime
Avoid continuous lowland cropping on acid-Fe soils
severityGuidance: Medium when bronze spots only at leaf tips; High when whole plant bronzed and stunted
farmerFriendlySummary: Rice leaves turning bronze in flooded fields — likely iron toxicity. Drain briefly and lime the field.

name: Aluminum Toxicity
symptoms: Stunted root growth — short, thick, brown roots
Phosphorus deficiency symptoms appearing despite adequate P
Stunted whole plant with poor yield
Drought sensitivity due to limited root depth
commonCauses: Acidic soils (pH below 5.0) releasing soluble Al
Highly weathered tropical Oxisols and Ultisols
Continuous acidifying N fertilisation without lime correction
treatment: Lime to raise soil pH toward 5.5-6.5 (critical)
Gypsum to displace Al deeper in subsoil
Plant Al-tolerant varieties (Brachiaria, certain rice and sorghum)
Phosphate fertilisation to immobilise Al
prevention: Annual soil pH test and lime correction
Cover crops with deep roots that tolerate Al
Use Al-tolerant varieties on chronically acid sites
severityGuidance: Medium when roots short but plant living; High when whole-plant stunting and yield collapse
farmerFriendlySummary: Roots are stunted and plant suffers in acid soil — aluminium toxicity. Lime the field.

name: Salinity Stress
symptoms: White salt crust on soil surface
commonCauses: Poor irrigation drainage in dry climates
Heavy use of mineral fertilisers raising soil EC
treatment: Heavy leaching irrigation with clean water (where possible)
Gypsum application to displace Na on cation sites
Improve drainage to remove leached salts
Plant salt-tolerant varieties (Pokkali rice, certain barley, date palm)
prevention: Test irrigation water EC and choose source carefully
Periodic leaching to prevent salt build-up
Mulch to reduce evaporation-driven salt concentration
severityGuidance: Medium when only tip burn; High when whole-plant stunting and yield loss
farmerFriendlySummary: Crops stunted despite enough water, white crust on soil — too much salt. Improve drainage and leach.

name: Low Organic Matter
treatment: Apply compost (5-10 tons/ha annually)
Apply aged manure
Green manure cover crops (mucuna, sun hemp)
Reduced tillage / conservation agriculture
prevention: Agroforestry — tree-crop intercrops cycle deep OM
severityGuidance: Medium when fertiliser response declining; High when soil visibly degraded and erosion present
farmerFriendlySummary: Soil looks tired and fertiliser doesn't work as well — needs more organic matter. Add compost and stop burning residues.

name: Soil Acidity
symptoms: Aluminium and manganese toxicity symptoms appearing
commonCauses: Continuous use of ammonium-based N fertilisers (urea, NH4)
Lack of liming over multiple seasons
treatment: Apply agricultural lime (CaCO3) — 1-3 tons/ha depending on soil test
Use dolomitic lime when Mg also low
Wood ash as low-cost lime alternative
Plant pH-tolerant varieties as bridge
prevention: Annual or biannual soil pH test
Balance fertiliser N sources (mix ammonium with nitrate)
Use leguminous cover crops to fix N without acidification
severityGuidance: Medium when crops still respond to fertiliser; High when whole-field stunting and Al toxicity
farmerFriendlySummary: Soil is too acidic — crops won't take up nutrients. Test soil pH and add lime.
